summary: Verified a real narrow fix for empty finished-request insertion and resource/lock ownership in the active UnifiedRadixCache path. This is a partial original-issue fix; the reported long-uptime Qwen4Exp NEXTN acceptance decay was not reproducible in the available architecture and model environment.

Candidate regression on exact candidate source: 4 passed, covering empty finish cleanup, non-empty boundary insertion, zero-length finish, and direct empty insert.
10 passed, including independent 256-request accumulation/resource stability and existing matched-node preservation cases.
37 passed and 2 subtests passed across cache selection, lock-reference, and Mamba state-cap adjacent behavior.

gpu_evidence: PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 reported CUDA-compatible execution on AMD Instinct MI355X, gcnArchName gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-. GPU-backed cache fixtures executed in all regression and adversarial tests.
native_rebuild_reason: Candidate changes only Python source and tests; repository-environment.json records native=null and wheel=null. Source imports were confirmed from /job/repo/python, so no native rebuild was applicable.
remaining_counterexamples: No 16-24 hour Qwen3.8/Qwen4Exp NVFP4 NEXTN serving run was possible, so acceptance decay may persist through another path.

The upstream issue records a relapse after both speculative clamp sites and the legacy cache fix, establishing that those fixes alone were insufficient but not proving this unified-cache fix is sufficient.
The reported NVIDIA SM121, two-node TP=2 architecture was not tested; this review used one AMD gfx950 GPU.
No model weights were available, so model semantics, throughput restoration, restart recovery, multi-node behavior, and full HTTP serving behavior remain unverified.
